label: Data-driven business questions
text: A marketing research analyst testing a new television advertisement; a pharmaceutical manufacturer comparing a new drug; an operations manager checking product quality; a software company reviewing call-centre satisfaction; management assessing 1st year MBA students in LMTSM.

label: Shark attacks and ice-cream sales
text: Both rise and fall together through the year because summer drives both: a spurious correlation.

label: Employee attrition rate
text: A statistician's model concluded that employees below the age of 30 who live 20+ miles from work do not stay long.

label: Retailer and HR examples
text: A retailer uses sales data to decide inventory stocking; HR managers use attrition statistics to plan hiring.

label: Quantitative techniques by function
text: Marketing: survey data to choose the most effective advertising channel. Finance: predicting stock price movements with time series analysis. Operations: route optimisation to minimise fuel costs. Human Resources: employee satisfaction survey data to improve retention.

label: Restaurant chain
text: A restaurant chain analyzes customer visit data to identify peak business hours and plan staffing.

label: Graph A (AIM) and Graph B (QTM)
text: Two class-performance curves: AIM peaks towards the right with a long left tail; QTM peaks towards the left with a long right tail.

label: Census and exit poll
text: Census is the example of descriptive statistics; exit poll is the example of inferential statistics.

label: Population and sample pairs
text: Songs from Bollywood movies (population) vs those that won the National Award (sample); participants of PGP in LMTSM vs those with less than 1 years of experience.

label: Florida Department of Tourism survey
text: Telephone survey of in-state residents; stratified by north, central and south Florida; random digit dialing; next-birthday method; sample size 868.

label: Sampling method examples
text: 200 of 2000 students (simple random); 25 of 500 students (systematic); India's N, S, W, E regions (stratified); a school's branches and TIET's departments (clustered).

label: CIGNA retirement services survey
text: Telephone survey by Gfk NOP World of 659 full-time employees over 18, 80 percent in a retirement plan; stratified by income and age.

label: Grouped classifications
text: Weight classes 40-45 to 95-100; marginal, small, medium and big farmers by hectares; revised MSME classification; education levels E0 to E5.

label: Runners and the four scales
text: Runner numbers (nominal), finishing places (ordinal), 0-to-10 performance ratings (interval), finishing time in seconds (ratio).

label: Customer details table
text: Customers A to G with salary, age, gender and family size, used to label record, data set, variable, discrete, continuous, qualitative and quantitative.

label: Survey questions classified
text: Facebook profile yes/no (categorical), text messages in three days (numerical discrete), app download time in seconds (numerical continuous).
